title: SCA Minhag of the Week 178: "Flowers on Sebbit Day"

chapters.title: Flowers in the Synagogue for Shabbat
chapters.about: Sending flower arrangements to the synagogue for happy occasions on Shabbat morning.

chapters.title: The Women's Minhag of Decorating Rimonim
chapters.about: The involvement of mothers, grandmothers, and aunts in bringing flowers for the occasion.

chapters.title: Preparing Flowers on Friday
chapters.about: Women coming to the synagogue on Friday to attach simple, hardy flowers to the rimonim.

chapters.title: Carrying the Decorated Sefer Torah
chapters.about: Fathers and grooms carrying the Sefer Torah with decorated rimonim during services.

chapters.title: Bringing Back the Minhag
chapters.about: The significance of this generational minhag and the hope to revive it.

summary: Mr. Mosseri discusses the custom of using flowers to adorn the synagogue and the rimonim on the Sefer Torah for happy family occasions on Shabbat. He explains how mothers, grandmothers, and aunts would come to the synagogue on Friday to attach simple flowers to the rimonim with thin metal twist ties. This former community practice added excitement and pride for the women involved, and Mr. Mosseri expresses a desire to see this minhag brought back.
questions: What is the custom of sending flowers to the synagogue before Shabbat?
How were women involved in decorating the Torah for family occasions in the past?
What kind of flowers and materials were used to decorate the rimonim?
How did the community know when a family had a happy occasion in the synagogue?
